2609.19549.title: Finding Common Ground: Graded Communal Knowledge in Bluesky Starter Packs
2609.19549.paper_summary: Communication is made possible by common ground---the unspoken knowledge that people share and presuppose of one another, whether that be online or offline. In his conception of common ground, Clark (1996) distinguishes between personal and communal common ground, and asserts that the latter is graded: the more community affiliations two people share, the more common ground they share as well. Social media research has invoked this mechanism to explain how users connect, but it has gone largely untested because community memberships are rarely visible and, where they are, they are coupled to user interactions in a way that leads to conflating effects. To circumvent these challenges, this study repurposes Bluesky starter packs (SPs) as user-curated community affiliation labels. Across 191,648 pairs of users, we show that shared lexical repertoire---our proxy for common ground---grows monotonically with the number of SPs that users share, with users sharing a single pack being roughly twice as similar as equally connected strangers. A semantic renormalization of SP co-membership shows furthermore that it is more so the number of topically \emph{distinct} communities, rather than the raw count, in which common ground is graded. Finally, we show that community co-membership adds to common ground independently of proximity in the Bluesky follow network. These results lead to the conclusion that community membership is a measurable, separable, and semantically structured carrier of common ground. Reading it as such makes common ground observable before an exchange rather than inferred from it, and thus opens the door for large-scale observational approaches to a set of questions that have so far only been posed in the laboratory.
2609.19549.paper_summary_zh: 溝通的可能性源於共同基礎——人們彼此共享和預設的默默知識，無論是在線上還是線下。在他對共同基礎的概念中，Clark (1996) 區分了個人共同基礎和社群共同基礎，並主張後者是有層次的：兩個人共享的社群聯繫越多，他們共享的共同基礎也越多。社交媒體研究已經引用了這一機制來解釋用戶如何連接，但由於社群成員資格通常不易察覺，且在可見的情況下，它們與用戶互動的方式會導致混淆效應，因此這一機制在很大程度上未經測試。為了克服這些挑戰，本研究將 Bluesky 入門包 (SPs) 重新用作用戶策劃的社群隸屬標籤。在 191,648 對用戶中，我們顯示共享的詞彙庫——我們對共同基礎的代理——隨著用戶共享的 SP 數量單調增長，分享單個包的用戶彼此之間的相似度大約是同樣連接的陌生人的兩倍。SP 共同成員資格的語義重正化進一步顯示，影響共同基礎的層次的更是主題上\emph{不同}社群的數量，而不是單純的計數。最後，我們顯示社群共同成員資格在 Bluesky 關注網絡中獨立於接近度地增加了共同基礎。這些結果得出結論，社群成員資格是一種可測量、可分離且具有語義結構的共同基礎載體。將其視為如此使得共同基礎在交換之前可觀察，而不是從中推斷，因此為一系列迄今僅在實驗室中提出的問題開啟了大規模觀察方法的大門。
